sourcedFrom: USER MANUAL FOR KGM RF22 SUPPRESSOR — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. (2025 — ©2025 on the title page.)
cleanIntro: A 5 oz .22 can that KGM designed to come apart — the spec table says "User Serviceable: Yes" and the book prints the teardown with its own tool. It is rated up to 5.7x28, which is why the interval is short: basic cleaning every 150–200 rounds, a full submerged clean at a thousand or once a year. ⛔ The internals are ALUMINIUM, so the chemistry matters — an aluminium-friendly solvent or nothing. And the one part that has an orientation is the steel blast baffle: its engraved arrow faces the muzzle.

steps.title: Host unloaded before the can is touched
steps.action: KGM's first safety line covers mounting, removing, cleaning, storage and shipping in one sentence — the gun is unloaded for all five. Magazine out, action open, chamber checked by eye and by finger.
steps.quote: Ensure the host firearm is UNLOADED before mounting or removing the suppressor, cleaning, storage, or shipping
steps.cite: USER MANUAL FOR KGM RF22 SUPPRESSOR — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM RF22 Suppressor User Manual — Safety Precautions, printed p.2

steps.title: ⛔ Cool before it comes off
steps.action: A .22 can run on 5.7x28 gets hotter than its size suggests. The book puts the wait in its own warning box above the removal procedure.
steps.quote: If suppressor is hot, wait for it to cool before attempting to remove.
steps.cite: USER MANUAL FOR KGM RF22 SUPPRESSOR — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM RF22 Suppressor User Manual — Removing Direct Thread Suppressor, printed p.5

steps.title: Off the muzzle by the grasping grooves
steps.action: Hold the can by the knurled grasping grooves, hold the gun, and unscrew counter-clockwise. If carbon has locked it on, KGM's own answer is a 7/8 inch wrench on the REAR MOUNT — not on the tube, and not on the front cap.
steps.aside: After extensive firing, carbon buildup can make the suppressor hard to remove. Use a 7/8” wrench on the rear mount to get additional leverage for removal.
steps.quote: Un-screw the suppressor in a counter-clockwise direction.
steps.cite: USER MANUAL FOR KGM RF22 SUPPRESSOR — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM RF22 Suppressor User Manual — Removing Direct Thread Suppressor, printed p.5

steps.title: Front cap off with the male end of the tool
steps.action: The RF22 ships with its own assembly/disassembly tool and it is double-ended. The male end goes into the front cap; unscrew counter-clockwise until the cap is off. Everything from here is what the cap was holding in.
steps.quote: Grasp the suppressor and insert male end of the RF22 Assembly/Disassembly tool into the front cap. Use the tool to unscrew counter-clockwise until the front cap is removed from the suppressor.
steps.cite: USER MANUAL FOR KGM RF22 SUPPRESSOR — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM RF22 Suppressor User Manual — Disassembly of RF22 Suppressor, printed p.7

steps.title: Baffles out — and catch them
steps.action: Tip it and they may simply fall out. Fouled, they stay put, and the fix is a WOOD OR DELRIN rod from the back end and a gentle push — soft rod, soft push, because the baffles are aluminium. Expect them to separate and come free as they clear the tube, so work over the bench, not over the floor.
steps.aside: The baffles may freely fall out, or if heavily fouled may stay in place.
steps.quote: If the baffles do not freely fall out, insert a wood or delrin rod from the back end. A gentle push will push the baffles out
steps.cite: USER MANUAL FOR KGM RF22 SUPPRESSOR — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM RF22 Suppressor User Manual — Disassembly of RF22 Suppressor, printed p.7

steps.title: Rear mount off with the female end
steps.action: The other end of the same tool takes the rear mount off, counter-clockwise. That is the whole can: tube, front cap, baffle stack, steel blast baffle and rear mount.
steps.quote: To remove the rear mount, attach the female end of the tool to the rear mount and unscrew counter-clockwise.
steps.cite: USER MANUAL FOR KGM RF22 SUPPRESSOR — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM RF22 Suppressor User Manual — Disassembly of RF22 Suppressor, printed p.7

steps.title: ⛔ Aluminium-friendly chemistry, nylon brush
steps.action: The baffles and front cap are aluminium and the wrong solvent will eat them. Nylon brush on the accessible surfaces, wipe everything down, then rinse and dry. That is the 150-to-200-round job.
steps.aside: KGM recommends basic cleaning every 150-200 rounds depending on the host firearm and ammunition.
steps.quote: Wipe down all surfaces, and use a nylon brush to eliminate carbon and copper fouling from accessible surfaces. If using chemicals, ensure they are not corrosive to aluminum.
steps.cite: USER MANUAL FOR KGM RF22 SUPPRESSOR — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM RF22 Suppressor User Manual — Regular Maintenance, printed p.10

steps.title: The heavy clean: submerged, rinsed, blown dry
steps.action: At a thousand rounds, once a year, or whenever it stops working as well: the parts go into a chemically resistant container and get submerged in an aluminium-friendly suppressor chemical. Then out, rinsed, brushed, rinsed again, and dried with compressed air before anything is reassembled.
steps.aside: Use compressed air to dry suppressor internals.
steps.quote: Using an aluminum-friendly suppressor cleaning chemical, fill the container until the suppressor parts are submerged.
steps.cite: USER MANUAL FOR KGM RF22 SUPPRESSOR — Rev: 1/25 — printed on the title page. — KGM RF22 Suppressor User Manual — Heavy Cleaning, printed p.10
steps.warn: Perform a more thorough cleaning cycle for the suppressor after one thousand rounds (1,000), on an annual basis, or as necessary due to fouling or loss of effectiveness.

deepAbsentReason: THE PUBLISHED TEARDOWN IS ALREADY THE WHOLE CAN, so there is nothing deeper to publish. KGM's field procedure takes the RF22 down to tube, front cap, baffle stack, blast baffle and rear mount — five parts and a tool — and a baffle does not itself come apart. The book's only escalation past that is the warranty route: an RMA number from Customer Service before anything is shipped. Inventing a deeper step would mean inventing a joint the product does not have.

cleaning.name: BAFFLE STACK AND FRONT CAP (ALUMINIUM)
tasks: ⛔ Aluminium-friendly chemicals ONLY — the wrong solvent eats them
Nylon brush on the accessible surfaces, carbon and copper
Submerged for the heavy clean, then rinsed with water
Compressed air through the internals before reassembly

cleaning.name: BLAST BAFFLE (STEEL) AND REAR MOUNT (TITANIUM)
tasks: Blast baffle cleaned and its ENGRAVED ARROW found before it goes back
Rear mount threads cleaned — this is the part a wrench is allowed on

cleaning.name: MOUNT AND THREADS
tasks: 1/2x28 barrel threads cleaned and checked undamaged
⛔ Mount fully contacting the barrel shoulder, no visible gap

cleaning.name: ⛔ THE INTERVALS ARE THE MAINTENANCE
tasks: Heavy clean at 1,000 rounds, annually, or on loss of effectiveness
Weigh it new and weigh it again periodically — KGM's own fouling measure

reassembly: Rear mount onto the rear of the tube, clockwise, snug with the female end of the tool.
⛔ Blast baffle first, closest to the rear mount, engraved ARROW FACING THE MUZZLE.
The aluminium baffles after it, cone end facing the rear — they need no indexing and no fixed order.
Front cap on with the male end of the tool, snug. It may not sit flush on a low-round can; that is by design.
Onto the host with the action open and clear: clockwise until it completely stops, then hand-checked for a firm seat.
A 7/8 inch or strap wrench on the REAR MOUNT only, if extra force is wanted.
First fitting on a new host: verify alignment with a bore rod, and REMOVE THE ROD BEFORE FIRING.
fncheck: Back together: rear mount snug with the tool, blast baffle nearest it with its engraved arrow pointing at the muzzle, the rest of the stack cone-end rearward, front cap snug. ⛔ A front cap that does not sit flush with the tube is NORMAL on a new or low-round can — KGM designs the stack to compress — so do not force it. Sight through the bore for one clear channel. On the host, screw it down until it stops and then try to turn it further by hand: it must be firmly seated, with the mount fully against the barrel shoulder and no visible gap. First time on a new host, check it with a bore alignment rod — and take the rod out before you fire.
